title: AI-Led Correction Deepens as Financing Fears Spread From Nvidia to Credit
content:
The AI trade that powered 2026 cracked decisively, as the sell-off broadened from a valuation wobble into a full index correction and a question over how the buildout is funded.

Across the four weeks the Nasdaq surrendered its entire 2026 gain and the S&P 500 and Dow fell into **correction**, logging the longest losing streak since early 2020. Nvidia was the fulcrum: a quarterly revenue beat near **$115.8bn** failed to halt a slide of more than **20%**, as leadership upheaval and scrutiny of **circular financing** between chipmakers, neoclouds and private credit hardened the mood. Even Anthropic's record IPO could not lift sentiment.

It mattered because AI is now the index and, increasingly, the credit market: regulators began probing how interconnected financing could amplify a downturn, widening high-yield spreads and lifting volatility. Nvidia's standing and private-credit resilience are the swing factors into year-end.

title: Hot CPI Puts a December Fed Hike, Possibly Supersized, Back in Play
content:
The higher-for-longer regime hardened into an outright hawkish bias, as a hot inflation print revived expectations that the Fed will tighten again before year-end.

A hotter-than-expected October CPI, rising **0.4%** on the month with sticky core services, pushed futures markets to price a December move as near-certain and briefly to flirt with a supersized **50bp** step. The repricing kept the 10-year UST near **4.95%** even as equities fell — an unusual pairing that showed policy expectations, not growth, were driving the curve.

It sat at the centre of everything: elevated real yields pressured the richest equities and underpinned the dollar, while reviving the long-end **term premium**. The 25 November PCE release is the pivotal catalyst that could confirm or defuse the December decision.

title: Havens Reshuffle as the Dollar and Treasuries Win and Gold's Bid Fails
content:
The risk-off wave forced a reshuffle of safe havens, and the winners were not those that had defined 2026. As equities fell, investors rotated into cash, the dollar and short-dated Treasuries rather than the metals that led the year.

The USD climbed to around a nineteen-month high, the index near **103.8**, while USTs drew a clear bid and yields eased across the curve. Gold, by contrast, failed as a hedge: it fell roughly **10%** into the sell-off and its correlation with equities turned positive, unwinding the **debasement hedge** that had powered its run.

It mattered as a regime signal — with the Fed expected to tighten, the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding metal rose just as liquidity was prized. A firmer dollar also squeezed emerging-market and commodity-linked currencies, tightening global financial conditions.

title: Crude Slumps Towards $90 as a Deepening Supply Glut Offsets Inflation
content:
Oil extended a sustained retreat as a growing supply overhang, not demand, set the tone, turning energy from an inflation threat into a mild disinflationary offset.

Brent fell roughly **15%** over the four weeks towards the low **$90s**, with WTI dropping faster, as rising non-OPEC output and softer demand signals deepened a visible **supply glut**. The slide ran against the firmer dollar and offered central banks only limited cover, since core services, not energy, now drive the inflation data.

It mattered as a cross-current: cheaper crude eased headline inflation at the margin even as the Fed leaned hawkish, while pressuring energy equities and commodity-linked currencies. Any renewed supply disruption or OPEC+ response remains the key upside risk into year-end.
